I need to write JUnit 4 tests for the abstract Axis class, so I'll create a concrete subclass implementing the abstract methods to test against. I'm continuing to map out test cases across the remaining properties: label font, paint, insets, angle, tooltip, and URL; axis line visibility, paint, and stroke; tick label visibility, font, paint, and insets; and tick mark visibility, lengths, stroke, and paint. For each, I'm noting the branches to cover, especially null checks that should throw exceptions and equals-comparison logic for change detection.

Beyond the getter/setter pairs, I still need coverage for plot association (which triggers configure), fixed dimension, listener management and notification, label enclosure calculation with its edge-dependent branching, the drawLabel and drawAxisLine methods across all four edge positions, plus clone, equals, and serialization round-trips. Given the sheer scope, I'm planning to build a minimal concrete TestAxis subclass with bare-bones implementations of the abstract methods, and I'll use a BufferedImage's Graphics2D context for testing the drawing-related methods that need a real graphics object.

Since the classpath assumes the full jfreechart project is available alongside junit and servlet.jar, I can freely use PlotRenderingInfo, ChartRenderingInfo, and EntityCollection in my tests. Building the concrete Axis subclass...

Now I'm adding a listener stub that tracks how many times it's been notified, then sketching test cases: checking constructor defaults, verifying visibility toggling only fires notifications when the value actually changes, and testing label-setting branches for equal versus differing values including null cases.

I also plan tests for label font (throwing on null, notifying only when the font actually changes) and label paint, noting that setLabelPaint appears to notify unconditionally on any non-null assignment without an equality check.

For label insets, angle, tooltip, and URL, I'm mapping out which setters guard against no-op changes versus always firing notifications regardless of equality - insets check equality, angle and tooltip/URL always notify unconditionally since there's no equals comparison in their code. Axis line visibility follows the same always-notify pattern with no branching condition at all.

Moving through the rest of the axis line and tick properties, I'm cataloging which have equality guards (paint changes, stroke, font, insets) versus which just always fire (stroke assignment, tick mark lengths since they're primitive floats with no null check possible). The visibility flags for tick labels and tick marks both branch on whether the new boolean differs from the current field value before notifying.

For the plot association, setPlot should trigger a configure() call and flip a configured flag, with getPlot returning the same instance; even setting plot to null should still invoke configure since there's no null guard there. The fixed dimension property is a plain getter/setter with no extra logic.

I'm also covering listener management -- adding and removing listeners toggles hasListener appropriately, and firing an event with multiple listeners attached increments each one's counter, verifying the loop over the listener list works with several entries. Then there's the label enclosure calculation: a null or empty label string should yield a default zero-sized rectangle, while a non-empty label like "abc" combined with edges like BOTTOM should produce a rectangle with actual positive dimensions.

For the LEFT edge case, I need to confirm the angle adjustment branch doesn't throw and still returns a proper non-empty rectangle, using a BufferedImage to obtain a Graphics2D context for rendering. Since getLabelEnclosure and related drawing methods are protected, I'm planning to add public wrapper methods in the TestAxis subclass that expose getLabelEnclosure, drawLabel, and drawAxisLine so the tests can call them directly. Then for drawLabel, I'm outlining cases: a null state throws IllegalArgumentException, and a null or empty label returns the state unchanged via an early return.

I'm mapping out the remaining drawLabel scenarios: for each edge (TOP, BOTTOM, LEFT, RIGHT) I want to verify the cursor actually moves in the corresponding direction by comparing state before and after. I also need to check that a null plotState skips entity handling without throwing, but I'm noticing a possible issue where if plotState is non-null but its owner is null, calling owner.getEntityCollection() would throw an NPE — this could be a known edge case tied to the original defect, so I want to be careful not to assume too much about the intended behavior here.

I decide the safest approach is to construct a real PlotRenderingInfo backed by an actual ChartRenderingInfo object rather than passing null, so I can test both when the entity collection is set and when it's left null by default, relying on the standard JFreeChart API methods for getting and setting the entity collection.

For dataArea and plotArea I'll use concrete Rectangle2D.Double instances with real dimensions. For drawAxisLine, since the axis line is drawn directly to the graphics context and not exposed, I can only confirm no exception is thrown rather than assert specific drawing behavior.

For equals(), I'm mapping out the many field checks that each return false on mismatch, meaning I need one fully-equal test case plus separate tests toggling each field individually to false to get reasonable branch coverage across that large method.

I'm planning a comprehensive test that builds two identical TestAxis instances, verifies they're equal, then mutates one field at a time (visible, label, labelFont, labelPaint, labelInsets, labelAngle, tooltip, URL, axis line settings, tick label settings, tick mark settings, fixedDimension) checking each toggle breaks equality and restoring it fixes it again, covering all the false-return branches plus the final true return.

I also need edge cases: comparing against null, against an unrelated object type, and against itself for reference equality. For clone(), I'll add a listener, clone the axis, and confirm the clone's plot is null and its listener list is reset even though the original still has a listener attached, while other fields remain equal but not identical by reference. For serialization, I'll write and read back an axis through byte streams to confirm the transient paint and stroke fields survive the custom writeObject/readObject logic, and I'll also check that labelToolTip and labelURL default to null.
